newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas seen stronger on storage buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas seen stronger on storage buying.

text.p: Canadian natural gas prices remained strong amid mild weather in western Canada on Wednesday, a situation which traders attributed to buying of supply for storage injection.
"I think there's storage buying happening -- people are trying to get some gas into the ground," a Calgary-based marketer said. "There's also a little California demand out there."
Spot gas at the AECO hub was quoted at C$1.475 per gigajoule, up from C$1.375/1.38 per GJ last week. April AECO was actively traded at C$1.50, up from C$1.39 last week.
At the borders, gas at Sumas was talked in the high US$1.10s per million British thermal units, unchanged from last week.

Traders said Sumas gas was difficult to come buy as sellers opted to make their deals at AECO or Westcoast Compressor Station 2. Station 2 was discussed at C$1.48 per gigajoule for spot and in the mid- to high- C$1.40s for April volumes.
At Niagara and Dawn in southern Ontario, gas prices were down about seven cents on the week to US$2.16 per mmBtu. April Dawn was quoted at US$2.13 per mmBtu.
